title: Signs, labels and organising the shop
summary: Finding things in a big shop is a design problem in Supermarket Simulator: the game gives signs their own icon and colour controls and puts labels on racks.
body: Signs are not decoration: the game lets you choose the icon and the colour a category sign carries, which is why a sign is a piece of information rather than a board.
Labels go on the racks themselves, so the shelf tells the customer what belongs there instead of leaving it to be discovered.
Even the shop's name can be set on an entrance sign, which is why the front of the shop is something you configure rather than accept.
What this entry does not tell you: how much signage changes customer behaviour or which icons exist. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Category signs carry an icon chosen from the game's own set.
Signs have a colour setting of their own.
The shop's entrance sign can be named.
The build ships its category sign materials and a closed sign of its own.
The sign palette is named in full, and includes London hue, lunar green, pale orange, pine glade, rock blue, sandrift and ship gray.
facts.evidence: asset names: M_CategorySign_London Hue, M_CategorySign_Lunar Green, M_CategorySign_Pale Orange, M_CategorySign_Pine Glade, M_CategorySign_Rock Blue, M_CategorySign_Sandrift, M_CategorySign_Ship Gray

facts.claim: Labels are shipped per place they belong to, with one for an item, one for a rack and one for a stall.
facts.evidence: asset names: Item Label, Rack Label, StallLabel

facts.claim: The label set also names blank coloured labels, a title ribbon, a left label and a liquor-shop label.
facts.evidence: asset names: Label_BasicLabel01_White, Label_TitleRibbon_Blue, Label_LeftLabel02, SM_LiquorShop_Label

facts.claim: A display stand is shipped for flyers, and the build names a flyer of its own with a second variant and an emissive sheet.
facts.evidence: asset names: SM_DisplayStand_Flyer, FlyerAsteroid, FlyerAsteroidB001, FlyerAsteroidEmissive

facts.claim: The signage artwork also includes a graffiti sheet and a cart logo, with a smoothness sheet for the road signs.
facts.evidence: asset names: T_Graffiti_2, Cart Logo, Road_Signs_MS

facts.claim: The game draws a department sign of its own for each part of the shop: book, breakfast, cleaning, dairy, pasta, meat, frozen, decoration, produce, toilet, water and wine.
facts.evidence: asset names: Sign1_Book, Sign2_Breakfast, Sign3_Cleaning, Sign4_Dairy, Sign5_Pastas, Sign6_Meat, Sign7_Frozen, Sign8_Decoration, Sign9_Produce, Sign10_Toilet, Sign11_Water, Sign12_Wine

facts.claim: The build also names price stands per department, with a deli, a green market, a liquor, a meat-and-dairy and a janitor's stand among them.
facts.evidence: asset names: SM_PriceStand_Deli, SM_PriceStand_GreenMarket, SM_PriceStand_Liquor, SM_PriceStand_MeatDiary, SM_PriceStand_Janitor

facts.claim: The shop's own signage runs to a closed sign, a sign board and a store entrance signboard, with a coloured version of the last.
facts.evidence: asset names: Closed Sign, M_SignBoard, M_StoreEntrance_Signboard, M_StoreEntrance_Signboard Colored, Conditioner_03_CloseSign

facts.claim: A walk-lane sign is named among the shop's own signs.
facts.evidence: asset name: M_ Walk Lane Sign
